classes.name: Alþingiskosningar
classes.finest_note: Statistics Iceland publishes list votes by constituency (8 constituencies 1959-1999, 6 since 2003) and only national totals before October 1959; votes by polling ward and by municipality are not published for Althing elections.
classes.locator: https://www.government.is/library/01-Ministries/Prime-Ministrers-Office/constitution_of_iceland.pdf (Art. 31: 63 members elected by proportional representation for four years, in no fewer than six and no more than seven constituencies)
classes.note: The Althing gained legislative power under the constitution of 1874; Statistics Iceland's series starts with the 1874 election. Single- and two-member constituencies until 1959 (with proportional representation in Reykjavík from 1920 and supplementary seats from 1934); eight multi-member constituencies with national adjustment seats from October 1959 (60 seats, 63 from 1987); six constituencies with 9 adjustment seats since 2003 (D'Hondt in each constituency, Arts. 109-110 of the Elections Act). The 1916-1930 elections of nationally elected members are the landskjor class.

classes.name: Landskjör til Alþingis
classes.name_en: Althing elections of nationally elected members
classes.note: Separate nationwide list elections of the Althing's nationally elected members (landskjörnir þingmenn), in which only voters aged 35 and over took part; abolished by the constitutional amendment that took effect for the 1934 election. The 23 October 1926 poll filled a single vacant seat.

classes.name: Aukakosningar til Alþingis
classes.note: Vacancies in the single- and two-member constituencies were filled by by-elections; from October 1959 a vacancy passes to the next substitute on the list (Elections Act Art. 111) and no by-election is held.
classes.disposition_reason: Statistics Iceland's election tables list general elections only (KOS01900 has no by-election rows), and no official list of the by-elections or their results was found; their returns sit in the Althing's own records (Alþingistíðindi) on althingi.is, which refused this session.

classes.name: Forsetakjör
classes.finest_note: Candidate votes by constituency (KOS07112 for 1952-1996, KOS07110 since 2004); turnout but not candidate votes by municipality from 2012 (KOS07002).
classes.locator: https://www.government.is/library/01-Ministries/Prime-Ministrers-Office/constitution_of_iceland.pdf (Arts. 3-7: elected by direct secret ballot; the candidate with the most votes is elected; a sole candidate is elected without a vote)
classes.note: Plurality, one round. Only contested elections are polled: a sole candidate is declared elected without a vote (Constitution Art. 5; Elections Act Art. 122), so the years with one candidate have no poll and no contest. The first president was chosen by the Althing in 1944 (class forseti_althingi).

classes.note: The Althing elected a regent (ríkisstjóri) to exercise the king's powers in 1941, 1942, and 1943, and on 17 June 1944, the day the republic's constitution took effect, elected the first President of Iceland for one year; every later president was elected by the people (Constitution Art. 3) or declared elected as the sole candidate.

classes.locator: https://www.stjornarradid.is/library/03-Verkefni/Kosningar/Kosningalog_enska.pdf (Art. 2: referendums the Althing decides on, and those under Arts. 11(3), 26, and 79(2) of the Constitution; Art. 26: timing)

Each question is one contest.

classes.name: Kosningar til ráðgjafarþings
classes.note: The restored Althing met from 1845 as a consultative assembly with members elected in the counties (sýslur) and Reykjavík until the constitution of 1874 gave it legislative power.
classes.disposition_reason: Statistics Iceland's series begins with the 1874 election (KOS02001: 'Participation in general elections to the Althingi 1874-2024'); no official publication of the 1844-1869 returns was found.

classes.name: Prófkjör
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose and rank their list candidates in primaries (prófkjör) or by their own councils, run under party rules; the Elections Act regulates only the lists submitted, and no public authority runs or publishes the primaries.

classes.name: Sveitarstjórnarkosningar
classes.finest_note: Each municipality elects its council at large; Statistics Iceland publishes list votes and seats by municipality from 2002 (KOS03210-KOS03214a) and Reykjavík's results from 1930 (KOS03107). Polling wards are not published.
classes.note: Restricted proportional (list) elections by D'Hondt where two or more lists stand, unrestricted personal elections where none does, and an uncontested (sjálfkjörið) list where only one does (Elections Act Arts. 116-118). A single national election day since 1962 (KOS03101); merged municipalities may elect a council off the cycle, as Múlaþing did on 19 September 2020.

classes.name: Kosningar til sýslunefnda
classes.note: Each rural municipality (hreppur) elected one member of its county council; the county councils were abolished at the end of 1988 and replaced by district committees named by the municipalities.
classes.disposition_reason: No official series of county council returns exists: Statistics Iceland's local tables (KOS02005, KOS03101) cover municipal councils only, and the returns were kept in each county's minutes.

classes.name: Kosningar innan þjóðkirkjunnar
classes.name_en: Church of Iceland elections (bishops, parish priests, church assembly)
classes.locator: https://www.government.is/library/01-Ministries/Prime-Ministrers-Office/constitution_of_iceland.pdf (Art. 79(2): a change to the status of the Church is put to a referendum; that referendum is in thjodaratkvaedi)
classes.disposition_reason: Elections of bishops, parish priests, and the church assembly are run by the Church of Iceland under its own rules for its members; they fill no public office and no public election authority runs or publishes them.
